easy.q: According to Elder Giuffra, what do we show the Lord when we obey the law of tithing?
options: That we trust Him
That we have plenty of money
That we can manage on our own
easy.why: Elder Giuffra testified that “the law of tithing is a law of faith.” When we obey it, we show our trust in the Lord.

easy.q: As a young missionary in Chile, whom did Elder Giuffra and his companion teach in this story?
options: A schoolteacher who lived by herself
A woman of about 70 who lived with her son
A young father who worked on a fishing boat
easy.why: In the city of Puerto Montt they taught a woman of about 70 who lived with her son, a member of the Church. They repeated each lesson twice to help her remember.

easy.q: Why did the sister in Chile think she would never be able to pay tithing?
options: Her son had asked her to wait
She did not believe the missionaries
She earned barely enough to live on
easy.why: She cleaned houses and washed clothes, and what she earned was barely enough for rent, a little firewood and some food.

easy.q: What did the sister do the night before the missionaries came back to her home?
options: She knelt and asked Heavenly Father to help her
She asked her neighbors to lend her money
She decided to put off her baptism for a year
easy.why: She told Heavenly Father she truly wanted to join His Church and that “He would need to help me live this law.”

easy.q: After the sister was baptized, what did her bishop tell Elder Giuffra about her?
options: She had moved away to another city
She came every week with her tithing envelope
She had become a teacher in the Primary
easy.why: Her bishop said she arrived every week with her tithing envelope and brought a fast offering on the first Sunday of each month.

medium.q: When the sister told the missionaries about her prayer, they felt peace and assurance. What did Elder Giuffra say they knew?
options: Her son had persuaded her to change her mind
She had found better-paying work that week
The Lord had heard both her prayers and theirs
Their mission president had visited her home
medium.why: The missionaries had prayed and fasted, and she had knelt in prayer. Elder Giuffra said, “We knew that the Lord had heard both her prayers and ours.”

medium.q: What principle does Elder Giuffra say his wife often teaches in their family?
options: We keep the commandments because we love God
We keep the commandments mainly to be blessed
We keep the commandments so trials will pass us by
We keep the commandments to set a good example
medium.why: Her teaching is that we obey “because we love God, not merely because we hope to receive the blessings that come from obedience.”

medium.q: In the words of President Russell M. Nelson that Elder Giuffra quoted, why is tithing preached to the poor people of the world?
options: So that every member of the Church will give the very same amount
Because the needs of the Church are greatest in the poorest nations
So that families will learn to budget what little they have with care
Because poverty goes on, generation after generation, until they pay tithing
medium.why: President Nelson said poverty “continues from one generation to another, until people pay their tithing.” Elder Giuffra introduced this by saying President Nelson taught that “tithing can break cycles of poverty in poor nations and families.”

medium.q: How do Elder Giuffra's years of service in Central America support President Nelson's teaching about tithing?
options: He saw poverty end wherever a chapel was built
He saw families move from want to greater stability
He saw members grow wealthy without much effort
He saw that schooling alone lifts families from want
medium.why: He has met families “who once worried about their next meal but who now enjoy greater stability,” prospering both temporally and spiritually.

medium.q: Elder Giuffra quoted the Lord's words “prove me now herewith.” What does the Lord promise there to those who bring their tithes?
options: To return ten times what they have given
To take away their trials and hardships
To open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing
To repay them fully in the life to come
medium.why: The Lord invites us to prove Him and see “if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing.”

hard.q: In the words of President Dallin H. Oaks that Elder Giuffra quoted, tithe paying is evidence of what?
options: That we already live the law of consecration
That we accept the law of sacrifice
That we have been blessed with prosperity
That we have set aside all worldly cares
hard.why: President Oaks taught that “Tithe paying is evidence that we accept the law of sacrifice.” It prepares us for the law of consecration; it is not yet that law.

hard.q: How did Elder Giuffra describe the sister's reasons for thinking she could never pay tithing?
options: They showed she was not yet ready for baptism
They were excuses she had learned from others
They proved the law could not apply to her
They made sense from a worldly perspective
hard.why: He did not dismiss her worry: “Everything she said made sense from a worldly perspective.” Tithing asks for faith that looks beyond that perspective.

hard.q: A faithful tithe payer loses his job. Which response best fits what Elder Giuffra taught about trials?
options: Trust that the Lord knows his circumstances and honors his obedience
Conclude that his tithing must have fallen short in some way
Set tithing aside until his family's income returns
Expect a better job soon as the reward he has earned
hard.why: Elder Giuffra said obedience does not free us from trials, yet the Lord “knows our circumstances, honors our obedience, and fulfills His promises in His own time and way.”

hard.q: Elder Giuffra wondered whether the Lord might have an exception for the sister. How did President Caballero's reply reframe that idea?
options: An exception could come only from her bishop
An exception would be unfair to other members
An exception would deny her the law's blessings
An exception might be right after her baptism
hard.why: He said, “you are no one to deny this sister the blessings of the law of tithing.” Excusing her would not have been a kindness; it would have withheld blessings.

hard.q: What does Elder Giuffra say about his own tithing in the years just after his baptism?
options: He paid only a part until his mission taught him more
He understood it well but had no income to tithe
He paid in full but did not fully grasp its promises
He doubted its promises until blessings began to come
hard.why: With summer jobs he paid full tithes and fast offerings, yet he “did not fully understand the meaning of the promises and blessings” until he taught the law as a missionary.
